title: UC10 Document Anonymizer
text:
0.1 What gets masked
Research with interviews, case files or theses runs into the same problem every time: the material names people and the organisation the research was for, and it cannot be shared until those are removed. Doing that by hand is slow and error-prone, and cloud anonymisation services mean sending the raw documents out of the organisation first.
UC10 does it locally. A PDF or Word file goes in; the same file comes out with the names of people (and their email, phone, student number and bank account) and the target company replaced by stable labels. Layout, tables and fonts stay as they were. Everything else stays readable: other organisations, software, places, dates, and the literature the document cites.
Not masked: other organisations, software (ERP, PLM), places, dates, job titles, and published references (“(Yin, 2018)” and the reference list). The target company is masked there too.
Labels are global and stable: the same person gets the same label in every document. Neo4j keeps a SHA-256 hash of each value with its label; the value itself is never stored.

title: UC10 Document Anonymizer
text:
0.2 Privacy design

Everything runs on the local machine in Docker: Docling, the anonymizer and Neo4j. During a 46-page run every connection stayed inside the local Docker network; host ports listen on 127.0.0.1 only.
Not yet enforced by the network: the containers could reach the internet. Blocking that is requested.
The written file is read back; if any original is still in it, no file is produced.
The key (keys/) reverses the anonymization, so it is personal data: it is kept apart from output/ and out of git.
The repo folder is synced by Nextcloud, so originals and keys also reach the Nextcloud server.
A Dutch one-pager for users: output/Onepager - lokaal anonimiseren.pdf.

title: 3  Architecture
text:
3.1 What is anonymized
Two things, decided 2026-10-01:
Everything else stays readable: other organisations, software (ERP, PLM), places, dates, job titles, and published references (the reference list and author-year citations like “(Yin, 2018)”). The target company is masked there too, because a cited company report would give it away.

title: 3  Architecture
text:
People: names (full names, and a surname used on its own later), plus what identifies a person directly: email address, phone number, student or employee number, bank account (IBAN).
The target company: the organisation the research was done for, named by the user in input/targets.txt (one company per line, other names of the same company after |).

title: 3  Architecture
text:
3.2 Data flow (local stack)
input/<name>.pdf|docx + input/targets.txt
        |
        v
scripts/anonymize_folder.py  ──POST /anonymize?document=true&targets=…──>  uc10-anonymizer (127.0.0.1:5010)
                                                                              |
  1. Docling (docling:5001, async API, pdf_backend pypdfium2, no OCR)  <──────+  PDF/DOCX → markdown
  2. Detection on the markdown (Presidio + spaCy nl_core_news_lg / en_core_web_lg)
       - markdown stripped for the NER (bold markers, one table cell per line), offsets mapped back
       - per-line language routing; long texts analysed in 50k-character chunks
       - organisations and places are detected only to win overlaps against wrong person guesses,
         then dropped; common words, defined abbreviations and respondent codes are not names
       - reference section and citations are protected
  3. Second detection pass on the file's own text (PDF text layer / Word paragraphs):
       Docling sometimes writes text differently ("22-06-2026" became a list item)
  4. Target company names (all given aliases), surnames of detected full names
  5. Labels from Neo4j (neo4j:7687): hash(type|value) → PERSOON_n / ID_n / ORGANISATIE_n, global and stable
  6. Rewrite the original file:
       DOCX: text replaced inside the Word XML across runs (body, tables, headers, footers, footnotes,
             comments, tracked changes, field codes, hyperlinks); author properties and comment authors removed
       PDF:  text redacted with PyMuPDF (removed, not covered), label drawn in an embedded font in the
             original size and colour; PII links, comments, forms, bookmarks, metadata, attachments and
             the structure tree removed
  7. Read-back check: if any original is still in the written file, no document is returned
        |
        v
output/<name with people and target masked>_anon.pdf        (non-PDF input: output/<name>/)
keys/<name>.<ext>.entity_map.json, keys/done.json           (the key; personal data, not shared)

title: 3  Architecture
text:
3.3 Privacy design

The service connects only to Docling and Neo4j. During a 46-page run, every connection of the anonymizer and Docling stayed inside the local Docker network. Host ports are bound to 127.0.0.1.
Not yet enforced: the containers can reach the internet. Network isolation is requested in InstallLocalAiPackage/REQUEST-uc10-network-isolation.md.
Neo4j stores a SHA-256 hash, the label and the type; never the original value.
The entity map reverses the anonymization, so it is personal data: it is written to keys/, apart from output/, and kept out of git.
The repo folder is in Nextcloud, so input/, output/ and keys/ are synced to the Nextcloud server.
Users get a Dutch one-pager on this: output/Onepager - lokaal anonimiseren.pdf (source docs/onepager-lokaal.html).

title: 3  Architecture
text:
3.4 Service

service/app.py, FastAPI; localstack container uc10-anonymizer (Dockerfile in InstallLocalAiPackage builds from this repo’s service/). Rebuild after a change: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.laptop.yml up -d --build --no-deps uc10-anonymizer
Dependencies: presidio 2.2.356, spaCy 3.7.6 with nl_core_news_lg 3.7.0 and en_core_web_lg 3.7.1, PyMuPDF 1.26.4 (AGPL: fine internally, decide before distributing), pymupdf-fonts, lxml, pyspellchecker.
Memory: 3 GB limit, ~1.7 GB in use (both LG models; 1.5 GB OOM-kills them).

4.3 Goal
A fully local anonymiser for research documents: a PDF or DOCX goes in, and the same document comes out with the names of people (and their email, phone, student number, bank account) and the target company replaced by stable labels (PERSOON_1, ORGANISATIE_1, …), layout intact. title: 4  Plan
text:
4.7 Epic 2: Consistent and measured
Working software: Labels are stable across documents; Dutch identifiers are caught; precision and recall are reported on every dry-run.
Demo: Run the evaluation set: per-type precision/recall in test-results/ JSON; the same name gets the same label in two files.
Requires: presidio, neo4j · Dutch recognisers, evaluation set

4.7.1 T2 — Stable labels with global consistency ✅ DONE
Done when: the same input always gets the same label across uploads (Neo4j LabelCounter).


4.7.2 T6 — Dutch identifier recognisers
What: Presidio pattern recognisers for BSN (with 11-proof), IBAN, postcode, KvK, licence plate. Done when: each type is detected in the test set.


4.7.3 T7 — Evaluation set and metrics
First real document (2026-09-30): a 46-page English master’s thesis (PDF, plus a DOCX made from it). Author, student number, supervisors and submission date are all removed from both outputs. Findings: - Heavy over-masking by the English NER: capitalised terms become ORGANISATIE/PERSOON (“Bill of Materials”, “Submission”, “Second”), journal names and cited authors in the reference list too. Safe but hurts readability. Decided 2026-09-30: published references stay readable. The reference section (heading up to the next heading/appendix) and author-year citations (“(Yin, 2018)”, “Eisenhardt (1989)”) are not detected or replaced; appendices are. Thesis: 669 → 177 masked values. Eval case cite-en guards this. - Over-masking of title-case words fixed 2026-09-30 (thesis: 177 → 59 masked values): - an NER guess whose every word also occurs in lowercase in the same document is a common word (“Submission”, “Engineering”, “Planning & Control”); emails/URLs don’t count, and a word that is part of a detected full name stays a name (“Volgens Bakker” after “Jan Bakker”); rule-based results are never dropped; - abbreviations the document defines from common words (“Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)”), technical terms like eBOM/mBOM, and respondent codes (R1–R11) stay readable; - surnames used on their own get the full name’s label (“De Vries said” → PERSOON_3); - written-out dates in both languages are a pattern rule now (“12 May 2026” on a line without context was missed). Eval cases title-words and nl-surname-words guard this. Still masked on purpose: interviewee job titles (quasi-identifiers in a single-company case). Still over-masked: single title words that never occur in lowercase in the document (“Master”, “Submission”) and concepts like “Bill of Materials” when “bill” never does. Known trade-off: an organisation whose name is only common words (“Beter Wonen”) is left readable unless a rule catches it (“Stichting Beter Wonen”, “… BV”). - Text in images (the university logo) is not touched. - Hyphenation at PDF line breaks: Docling joins the word, the file keeps the hyphen; reported as “not found in the file” (6 values in the thesis, none personal data). - Docling needs ~6 s per page on CPU (OCR off): 4-5 minutes for the thesis. - File names hold names too (“Thesis Eva Jansen - Voorbeeldbedrijf.pdf”). Decided 2026-09-30: output is output/<name>_anon.pdf (the original name, readable, by choice); non-PDF outputs in output/<name>/; entity maps (the keys) in keys/, apart from output/ so that folder can be shared. - Labels in PDFs: embedded font (the document’s own when it has the glyphs, else Noto Sans), original size and colour; too wide → squeezed, then shrunk (floor 40 %). Short originals (citations “Yin, 2018”, terms like “ETO”) still get small labels: a 10-15 character label in the space of 2-4 characters. What: 20 annotated documents (NL + EN) with expected entities; script that reports precision/recall per type. Done when: metrics are reported per run and targets are agreed.


4.7.4 T4 — Dry-run writes JSON results 🟡 IN PROGRESS
What: tests/dry_run.py writes test-results/dry_run_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.json with named steps. Done when: the ResearchReady workbook shows UC10’s dry-run. Status (2026-09-30): JSON written (13 checks, incl. DOCX + PDF via Docling and a leftover-fragment check). Workbook part ⛔ until the server is back.

title: 4  Plan
text:
4.8 Epic 3: Documents in, documents out
Working software: A DOCX or PDF goes in and the same format comes out, anonymised, with headings and tables intact.
Demo: Anonymise a DOCX with a table; open the result in Word.
Requires: docling, docconvert

4.8.1 T3 — Restore Docling on CT107
What: bring CT107 back (shared with UC1); keep the plain-text fallback. Done when: the dry-run’s Docling step passes and layout-aware markdown is used again.


4.8.2 T5 — Rebuild the document 🟡 IN PROGRESS
What: replace spans in the Docling markdown and convert back with docconvert CT122 (DOCX) or render PDF. Changed 2026-09-30: the entity map is applied to the original file (/anonymize?document=true), so docconvert is not needed. DOCX: text replaced in the Word XML (body, tables, headers/footers, footnotes, comments, tracked changes, field codes, hyperlinks); author/company properties and comment authors removed. PDF: text redacted (removed) with PyMuPDF and the label written in its place; links with PII, comments, form fields, bookmarks, attachments, metadata and the structure tree removed. The service reads the file back and returns no document if any original is still in it. Done when: a DOCX in gives an anonymised DOCX out with headings and tables intact. ✅ DOCX and PDF (dry-run step 8). Still open: test on real research documents; scanned PDFs are refused (no OCR redaction); a surname hyphenated across a PDF line break is not matched (the read-back check does not catch that either); PyMuPDF is AGPL (fine for internal use, decide before distributing).

4.9.1 T8 — Langfuse audit trace
Done when: one trace per document with a span per entity (type, hash, label — never the original).


4.9.2 T9 — Encrypted storage in MinIO
Done when: output and entity map stored in bucket doc-anonymizer with server-side encryption.


4.9.3 T10 — Versioned output in Gitea

title: 4  Plan

4.10 Epic 5: Researchers use it
Working software: Researchers anonymise files without curl, and interview transcripts keep speaker roles.
Demo: A researcher uploads a transcript and gets INTERVIEWER_1 / RESPONDENT_1 labels.
Requires: openwebui or n8n

4.10.1 T11 — Upload entry point
What: a simple upload page, or an OpenWebUI tool / n8n webhook, for researchers. Done when: a researcher can anonymise a file without curl.


4.10.2 T12 — Role-aware labels (phase 2)
What: detect speaker turns in interview transcripts and emit INTERVIEWER_1 / RESPONDENT_1. Done when: a transcript keeps who-said-what without names.
